messages:
marta: quick Q — for the upcoming canary, we want client-side opt-in A/B hooks. my rough idea: SDK exposes a tiny API and, when used, it adds an `x-redwood-variant` header on requests. example: `x-redwood-variant: canary-v2`.
kai: fwiw i'm worried about people spoofing headers if we just trust the client header. also privacy: canary telemetry might leak user cohort info unless opt-in is explicit.
adrian: +1 to explicit opt-in. what if SDK signs the header with a short HMAC tied to the API key? header could be `x-redwood-variant: canary-v2;sig=BASE64` and server verifies sig. keeps header trustworthy without server-side assignment.
lina: console/telemetry note — if we add variant dimension we need per-variant dashboards and quota split metrics. can we make the variant tag propagate into traces and cost breakdowns? otherwise ops won't know cost delta.
zoe: small perf/size note: keep header compact. also think about fallback semantics: server should never route a request to canary just because the header exists unless account is allowed (opt-in flag on account). so two-level guard: account opt-in + signed header.
adrian: agree on account-level allowlist. SDK flow:
```
// JS SDK
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: K });
// developer opts in explicitly
c.routing.setVariant({ name: 'canary-v2', signed: true });
```
server side verifies signature + account flag then applies routing.
kai: alternative: SDK only stores preference locally and we ask server on call whether to route. pros: zero-trust server-side decision. cons: extra roundtrip + complexity in client logic.
marta: that's helpful. i prefer signed header + server allowlist — cheaper to implement for now. Lina, can you confirm what slices the console needs? that's necessary for telemetry tagging.
lina: we need: per-variant token cost, latency p50/p95, error rate, and rollout % over time. also a quick filter on traces to compare canary vs prod. if header flows through tracing, we can build those pretty fast.
zoe: one more ops guard: if account has quota limits, routing must respect per-variant quotas (so a canary can't exceed quota by being routed there). i suggest we treat variant as a routing key that participates in quota checks.
adrian: security detail — HMAC key should be short-lived and rotated via the control plane. SDK fetches a signed token from control plane when developer enables variant in dashboard. avoids baking long-lived keys in client apps.
marta: OK action items:
- adrian: prototype header signing + server verification (POC by EOD Fri)
- lina: wire up console variant dimension + minimal dashboard (start Mon)
- zoe: quota/routing guard doc (how variant participates in quota checks)
- kai: short writeup on privacy implications & opt-in UX copy
we'll aim for 10% canary for 1 week if POCs look good. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: canary-v2 -> 10% traffic at 2026-04-02T14:00Z.
marta: thanks all — i'll link this thread to the rollout ticket.
